question:
A 25-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 2-week history of episodic bleeding from the nose and gums and one episode of blood in her urine. She was treated with chloramphenicol 1 month ago for Rickettsia rickettsii infection. Her pulse is 130/min, respirations are 22/min, and blood pressure is 105/70 mm Hg. Examination shows mucosal pallor, scattered petechiae, and ecchymoses on the extremities. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 6.3 g/dL
Hematocrit 26%
Leukocyte count 900/mm3 (30% neutrophils)
Platelet count 50,000/mm3
The physician recommends a blood transfusion and informs her of the risks and benefits. Which of the following red blood cell preparations will most significantly reduce the risk of transfusion-related cytomegalovirus infection?"?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Transfusion-related cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection risk" -> "CMV is transmitted through blood products" -> "Leukoreduction removes white blood cells" -> "White blood cells are a primary source of CMV" -> "Leukoreduced blood products significantly reduce CMV transmission risk" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Transfusion-related cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection risk" -> "CMV can be present in blood products" -> "Irradiation inactivates lymphocytes" -> "Lymphocytes can harbor CMV" -> "Irradiated blood products reduce CMV risk" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Transfusion-related cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection risk" -> "CMV is primarily found in leukocytes" -> "Washing blood products removes plasma and some cells" -> "Washing does not effectively remove all leukocytes" -> "Washing has limited impact on CMV risk" -> 60%

CHAIN: "Transfusion-related cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection risk" -> "CMV is transmitted through blood products" -> "Centrifugation separates components of blood" -> "Centrifugation does not remove leukocytes" -> "Centrifugation does not significantly reduce CMV risk" -> 50%

CHAIN: "Transfusion-related cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection risk" -> "CMV is transmitted through blood products" -> "Warming blood products is for patient comfort" -> "Warming does not affect leukocyte content" -> "Warming does not reduce CMV risk" -> 40%
analysis: Leukoreduction is a process that removes white blood cells from blood products, which significantly reduces the risk of transfusion-related cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection. CMV is primarily transmitted through leukocytes, so using leukoreduced blood products minimizes this risk. Other options like warming, washing, irradiation, and centrifugation do not specifically target the reduction of CMV transmission in the same way that leukoreduction does. Therefore, the best-supported option is leukoreduction.
